agree.reason: Starting with traffic and speaking as a neighbour two blocks away gives the two traffic-focused commissioners a reason to listen, but calling a C-to-D drop 'waiting a bit longer at a light' may come across as brushing off their main concern, and most opposed neighbours will not be moved.

honest.reason: All the numbers match the brief, 'nearly one in six' is a fair rounding of 64/412, and 'nothing gets torn down, no one gets moved out' follows reasonably from the land being a parking lot, though 'a little longer' softens a rush-hour rating drop that the speaker can't put a size on.

works_the_facts.reason: It works out the share of the waiting list (about one in six) and the parking ratio (over one space per unit), and it wisely leaves out the weaker 64-of-2,100 figure, but it doesn't reframe the 310 trips per day, which is roughly 5 per unit, spread across the whole day.

right_comparison.reason: It fairly sets the project against the status quo of an empty lot most of the week and a three-year wait, but it never says what that wait looks like for a household if nothing is built.

qualification.reason: The speech makes no conditional promises that need a checkable hedge, and it states the traffic impact plainly as fact.

objections.reason: The traffic objection is conceded honestly and weighed openly, and the parking worry is answered with the 72-space figure, but nothing speaks to whether the D rating could be mitigated, which is what the traffic-minded commissioners actually need.

fit.reason: At around 370 words in short spoken sentences with a clear ask at the start and end, it fits within three minutes at the podium.
